draft.change: Add Gen.9.8 as evidence for the existing addressee sense of אֶל at word index 0.
draft.definition: With a verb of speaking, אֶל introduces the addressee.
draft.evidence: In Gen.9.8, וְאֶל בָּנָיו adds Noah’s sons to the hearers already introduced by אֶל נֹחַ.

analysis.evidence: In אֶל הָאִשָּׁה אָמַר, “to the woman he said,” אֶל introduces the woman as the addressee of אָמַר.
analysis.sense: Marks the person or people addressed.

analysis.evidence: אֶל הָאִשָּׁה אָמַר means “he said to the woman.” The phrase identifies the addressee. Her marital relationship is expressed later by אִישֵׁךְ, “your husband.”
analysis.morphology: Definite article הָ־ prefixed to a feminine singular common noun in the absolute state.

analysis.evidence: אֶל הָאִשָּׁה identifies the woman as the addressee. אָמַר introduces the speaker’s own words, beginning הַרְבָּה אַרְבֶּה, “I will greatly multiply.”
analysis.morphology: Qal perfect, third person masculine singular, without prefix or suffix

analysis.evidence: הַרְבָּה immediately precedes אַרְבֶּה, the first-person singular Hiphil of the same verb. Together they mean “I will greatly increase.”
analysis.morphology: Hiphil infinitive absolute used to emphasize the following finite verb.
analysis.sense: cause to increase, used emphatically before the finite verb

analysis.evidence: In הַרְבָּה אַרְבֶּה, the preceding infinitive absolute emphasizes the finite verb, giving “I will greatly increase.” The direct objects עִצְּבוֹנֵךְ וְהֵרֹנֵךְ specify what the speaker will increase, and בְּעֶצֶב תֵּלְדִי בָנִים connects the pain with childbirth.
analysis.morphology: Hiphil imperfect, first person common singular. The initial א marks the speaker.
analysis.sense: cause to increase in amount or degree

analysis.evidence: The suffix ־ֵךְ refers to the woman being addressed. עִצְּבוֹנֵךְ is an object of הַרְבָּה אַרְבֶּה, “I will greatly increase.” The following words בְּעֶצֶב תֵּלְדִי בָנִים, “in pain you will bear children,” identify childbirth as the setting of her pain.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular noun in the construct state with a second-person feminine singular possessive suffix.

analysis.evidence: וְהֵרֹנֵךְ is coordinated with עִצְּבוֹנֵךְ “your pain” as a second object of אַרְבֶּה “I will multiply.” Both suffixes refer to the woman being addressed. The following words בְּעֶצֶב תֵּלְדִי בָנִים “in pain you will bear children” support the sense “pregnancy.”
analysis.morphology: Conjunction וְ prefixed to a masculine singular construct noun with a second-person feminine singular possessive suffix.

analysis.evidence: In בְּעֶצֶב תֵּלְדִי בָנִים, “in pain you will bear children,” בְּעֶצֶב describes the pain accompanying childbirth and echoes עִצְּבוֹנֵךְ, “your pain,” earlier in the verse.
analysis.morphology: The prefixed preposition בְּ governs the masculine singular absolute noun עֶצֶב.

analysis.evidence: The speaker addresses הָאִשָּׁה, the woman. In בְּעֶצֶב תֵּלְדִי בָנִים, בָנִים is the direct object of תֵּלְדִי, yielding “in pain you will bear children.”
analysis.morphology: Qal imperfect, second person feminine singular

draft.change: Add the use of אֶל with desire to the senses of the preposition in elah.
draft.definition: אֶל marks the person toward whom a desire is directed.
draft.evidence: In Genesis 3:16, אֶל אִישֵׁךְ gives the direction of תְּשׁוּקָתֵךְ.

analysis.evidence: In וְאֶל אִישֵׁךְ תְּשׁוּקָתֵךְ, “and toward your husband is your desire”, אֶל governs אִישֵׁךְ, “your husband”. The prepositional phrase comes before תְּשׁוּקָתֵךְ, “your desire”, and gives its direction.
analysis.morphology: Conjunction וְ “and” prefixed to the preposition אֶל “toward”, with no suffix.
analysis.sense: Marks the person toward whom desire is directed.

analysis.evidence: In וְאֶל אִישֵׁךְ תְּשׁוּקָתֵךְ, “your desire is toward your husband,” the suffix ־ֵךְ refers to the woman being addressed. The following וְהוּא, “and he,” refers back to her husband.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular noun in the construct state with a second-person feminine singular possessive suffix.

analysis.evidence: The suffix ֵךְ identifies the woman being addressed as the one who longs. The preceding phrase וְאֶל אִישֵׁךְ, “and toward your husband,” identifies the person toward whom her longing is directed.
analysis.morphology: Feminine singular noun in the construct state with a second-person feminine singular possessive suffix.

analysis.evidence: הוּא refers back to אִישֵׁךְ (“your husband”) and serves as the explicit subject of יִמְשָׁל בָּךְ (“will rule over you”).
analysis.morphology: Prefixed conjunction וְ plus independent third-person masculine singular pronoun הוּא.

analysis.evidence: In וְהוּא יִמְשָׁל בָּךְ, הוּא refers to the woman’s husband, and בָּךְ identifies the woman as the one over whom he will rule.
analysis.morphology: Qal imperfect, third person masculine singular.
